newsitem.title: USA: Two white rhinos died in China - San Diego Zoo.
newsitem.headline: Two white rhinos died in China - San Diego Zoo.

text.p: Two white rhinos donated by the San Diego Zoological Society to the Chengdu Zoo in China died of exposure and dehydration last summer during shipment, officials said Monday.
The July 31 deaths may mark a turning point in exchange programmes between the society and the Chinese government, Tom Hanscom, a spokesman for the Zoological Society, said.
The animals arrived in Shanghai on July 16 "healthy and alert," according to a message faxed by the director of the Shanghai Zoo to officials here. After that, "we lost control," said Hanscom.
While an agreement with the Chengdu Zoo specified the animals were to be shipped by rail, someone decided to ship them by truck to Chengdu, a 1,000-mile (1,600-km) journey.
Hanscom said the society would probably recommend that one of its representatives accompany any animals shipped to China in future, at Chinese expense.
"We're frustrated, and we voiced our frustration to the Chinese," Hanscom said. "We would not have sent the animals had we known the ground transportation had been altered."
The society had obtained the animals from the Pittsburgh Zoo after being contacted by the Chinese, who were looking for a male and female rhino to add to their breeding programme.

"They contacted us because we have the best record for breeding and managing white rhinos in the world," Hanscom said. Seventy-seven of the rare animals have been bred in captivity at the society's Wild Animal Park in Escondido, north of here.
Out of 67 rhinos the park has shipped all over the world, only one died, 18 years ago on its way to Taiwan.
Hanscom said the society learned of the July deaths the day after they happened but since the rhinos were Chinese property, "it was not our place to make an announcement."
He did not say why he was breaking the news now.
